answer: Per-identity proof-of-stake with slashing: each agent must post a base bond sized above one epoch of expected reward, and every attestation it files is verified only after random peers re-derive the evidence and compare it to a deterministic reference hash. A new duplicate identity needs real capital kept live for many epochs, so a farm of ten thousand puppets costs ten thousand stakes plus overhead, and equivocation burns the whole bond. That makes the mirror of an honest swarm pricier than its yield, while fluent sonnet-grade text fails the sampled onyx hash.
